items.title: Lab DNS server fails to bind a UDP+TCP port pair on Windows

labels.name: severity: medium
labels.description: Edge-case bugs, degraded behavior, meaningful maintenance cost

items.body:
## Summary
On Windows, `dnsserver` fails to start about a quarter of the time with "no free UDP+TCP port pair". Windows hands out consecutive UDP ports, so all 20 attempts land in the same TCP-reserved port block and every TCP bind fails. `-simulate-zone` (the labs) then exits 1, and the lab end-to-end tests fail intermittently on Windows.

## Where
- `internal/dnsserver/server.go:125-140` (UDP port chosen by the OS, then TCP bound on the same port, 20 attempts)

## Details
```go
for attempt := 0; attempt < 20; attempt++ {
    pc, err = lc.ListenPacket(ctx, "udp", net.JoinHostPort(host, "0"))
    ...
    ln, err = lc.Listen(ctx, "tcp", pc.LocalAddr().String())
    if err == nil { break }
    _ = pc.Close()
}
```

Running a lab scan 40 times on Windows 11 failed 10 times, each with ports that step by 20 (one run per attempt block):

```
Error: -simulate-zone: starting the local DNS server: no free UDP+TCP port pair: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:50121: bind: An attempt was made to access a socket in a way forbidden by its access permissions.
Error: ... listen tcp 127.0.0.1:50141: bind: ...
Error: ... listen tcp 127.0.0.1:50161: bind: ...
```

The OS's ephemeral UDP ports are sequential, so retrying with port 0 walks through one reserved TCP range (Hyper-V/WSL reservations, see `netsh int ipv4 show excludedportrange protocol=tcp`) rather than escaping it.

## Impact
Windows users of the labs (`-simulate-zone`) see random startup failures. `TestE2ELabTakeoverHint`, `TestE2ESARIF` and `TestDoTRejectsUntrustedCertificate` fail intermittently on Windows for this reason. This is a different cause from the timing flakes in #167.

## Steps to reproduce
1. On Windows with Hyper-V or WSL installed, build subenum.
2. Run `subenum -progress=false -type A,CNAME -simulate-zone examples/labs/lab1-first-scan.zone lab.example` 40 times in a loop.
3. Observe several "no free UDP+TCP port pair" failures with consecutive ports.

## Suggested fix
After a failed TCP bind, try an explicit random port in a high range (for example 20000-60000) for both UDP and TCP instead of asking the OS for another ephemeral UDP port. Alternatively, bind TCP first on a random port and fall back as now. Keep the attempt cap.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] 200 consecutive lab starts on Windows succeed
- [ ] A unit test in `internal/dnsserver` covers the retry path (for example, by injecting a listen function that fails the first N TCP binds)

## Getting started
- Relevant files: `internal/dnsserver/server.go`, `internal/dnsserver/server_test.go`
- How to run tests: `go test ./internal/dnsserver/ ./ -run 'Lab|SARIF'`
- Related: #167 (timing flakes, a separate cause), #170 (Windows CI)

---

items.title: release-snapshot CI step runs apt-get install without apt-get update

labels.name: severity: high
labels.description: Wrong results or crashes in common paths

items.body:
## Summary
The `release-snapshot` job's "Check completions and man page" step runs `apt-get install` without `apt-get update` first. The runner's package index is stale, so the install hits a 404 on an Ubuntu mirror, and the Go workflow has failed on every push to `main` since `c8134c6`, even though every test, lint and govulncheck job passes.

## Where
- `.github/workflows/go.yml:217` (`sudo apt-get install -y -qq zsh fish groff >/dev/null`)
- For comparison, `.github/workflows/go.yml:77-78` runs `apt-get update -qq` before its install

## Details
Failure log from the step:

```
E: Failed to fetch mirror+file:/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt/pool/main/p/pillow/python3-pil_12.1.1-2ubuntu1.3_amd64v3.deb  404  Not Found
E: Unable to fetch some archives, maybe run apt update or try with --fix-missing?
##[error]Process completed with exit code 100.
```

Every failing Go run from `c8134c6` to `e49aca4` fails only at `release-snapshot / Check completions and man page`. The last green run was `3139c44`.

## Impact
`main` shows red CI on every push, which hides real regressions and trains people to ignore the Go workflow. The completion and man-page syntax checks do not run.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Push any commit to `main`.
2. Open the Go workflow run: `release-snapshot` fails at "Check completions and man page" with apt exit code 100.

## Suggested fix
Add `sudo apt-get update -qq` before the install on line 217, and `--no-install-recommends` as the step at line 78 does. The `>/dev/null` also hides apt's error output in the log; consider dropping it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `release-snapshot` passes on `main`
- [ ] The step refreshes the package index before installing

## Getting started
- Relevant files: `.github/workflows/go.yml`
- How to run tests: push to a fork and watch the Go workflow, or run the step's commands in an `ubuntu-latest` container

items.title: Proposal: one storage format for timestamps and dates across the database
items.body:
## Summary

Date/time values are currently stored in several different text formats depending on which repository wrote them, because some repos format values themselves and others pass `time.Time` to the driver and get its default. This proposes one convention for the whole database, enforced through small Go types in the storage layer rather than per-query discipline.

This is a proposal for discussion; it changes how stored data is interpreted, so I'd like maintainer input before any PR.

## Current state

SQLite has no date/time storage class; `DATETIME` columns just get numeric affinity, and text that isn't a number stays text. What ends up stored is decided by each write path:

| How it's written | Example stored value | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `time.Time` to the driver, `.UTC()` first | `2026-10-22 06:24:41.0665941 +0000 UTC` | most `created_at`/`updated_at`, `audit_logs.timestamp` |
| `time.Time` to the driver, local time | `2026-10-22 04:34:17.0342307 -0700 PDT m=+0.0115` | timecard `clock_in`/`clock_out`, document `created_at` (#139) |
| `.Format(time.RFC3339)` | `2026-10-22T06:24:41Z` (seconds only) | appointments, notification log, reminder settings/rules, `patients.date_of_birth` |
| `YYYY-MM-DD` with `CHECK` | `2026-10-22` | `claims.date_of_service`, `payments.date` |

The driver format (`Time.String()`) is the modernc.org/sqlite default, kept by the driver only for backward compatibility, and it embeds the zone name and monotonic reading when given a local time. Text comparison is only correct when every row in a column uses the same format and zone.

## Proposed convention

Two different kinds of value, two formats:

1. **Instants** (created/updated, clock in/out, sent at, appointment start/end, audit timestamps): `INTEGER` Unix time in UTC. Zone-free, independent of driver defaults, numeric ordering, and still usable with SQLite date functions. Precision to decide: milliseconds (matches JS `Date` on the frontend) or nanoseconds. Same-tick ordering is handled by a tie-breaker regardless (see #138).
2. **Calendar dates** (date of birth, date of service, payment date): `TEXT` `YYYY-MM-DD`, never an instant. Storing a date of birth as UTC midnight is how birthdays shift by a day in some timezones. `patients.date_of_birth` currently stores `1990-05-01T00:00:00Z` and would move to the plain-date form like the billing columns.

## Enforcement

Add a small file in the storage layer (e.g. `internal/storage/sqlite/dbtime.go`) with two types implementing `driver.Valuer` and `sql.Scanner`:

- `Instant`: writes the canonical integer; reads **every legacy format** listed above (driver `String()` output including zone names and the `m=` suffix, RFC 3339, integers).
- `Date`: writes `YYYY-MM-DD`; reads `YYYY-MM-DD` and the RFC 3339 form currently used for date of birth.

Repositories switch to these types one domain area at a time. Because reads accept the legacy formats, this step needs no data migration and existing databases keep working; new writes are canonical from the first release that includes it.

## Out of scope here

Converting existing rows to the canonical forms is a separate data-migration step with its own risks (#141). Until it runs, columns contain a mix of legacy and canonical values, which is why the backfill should follow soon after, ideally in the same release.

## Open questions

- Integer instants vs fixed-width canonical UTC text (`2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z`): integer is more robust; text stays readable in the sqlite CLI.
- Millisecond vs nanosecond precision.
- Whether to also set `_time_format`/`_time_integer_format` in the DSN as a safety net for any `time.Time` that bypasses the types.

items.title: shield: proxy handler discards the upstream URL's path when forwarding requests
items.body:
In shieldProxyHandler in packages/guard/shield/shield.go, the line `target := *upstream; target.Path = r.URL.Path` (around line 122) overwrites the upstream URL's own Path field entirely with the incoming request's path, instead of joining the two. Any prefix configured on SOLONGATE_SHIELD_UPSTREAM or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, such as https://corp-proxy.example.com/llm, is silently dropped, and every proxied request goes to the upstream host's root path rather than under that prefix.

The fix is to join upstream.Path with r.URL.Path, for example with path.Join plus a check that the result keeps a leading slash, instead of assigning over target.Path.

items.title: Report source-frame reuse and measurement age without changing labels
items.body:
## Observed
New telemetry preserves per-pod source timestamps/windows (#42). In a separate verified three-capture baseline, all three AMF observations shared the same source timestamp and one-minute window even though capture times differed by about 16 seconds. Repeated averages are expected when polling faster than source updates, but row counts do not measure independent CPU observations.

## Scope
Propose a read-only diagnostic for source age, repeated frames and unknown legacy intervals. Keep the policy explicit and separate from labeling/model fitting. No cluster is needed; use synthetic JSONL fixtures.

## Acceptance
- Report per-pod known/unknown metadata, unique versus repeated timestamp/window frames, capture-to-source age and future/regressing source timestamps.
- Do not conflate identical values with identical source frames or claim repeated frames are necessarily unhealthy.
- Legacy source times stay unknown. Never invent a zero age/window or silently drop/relabel rows.
- Declare how name reuse, changed values for the same timestamp/window and clock skew are handled.
- Deterministic fixture reports, malformed-input rejection, preserved prior output on failure.
- Any later freshness/deduplication or measurement-time split policy needs its own documented decision and tests; this diagnostic alone does not establish train/test independence.

Start with internal/telemetry/measurement.go and docs/telemetry-and-dataset.md. Related: #33 for session holdouts.

items.title: feat(dashboard): keyboard shortcuts for search and navigation

labels.name: complexity:trivial
labels.description: Small, bounded change with obvious criteria (100 points)

items.body:
## Description

The UI is mouse-only. There are no keyboard shortcuts, and nothing focuses the search box on load, so every lookup starts by reaching for the pointer.

Search is the primary way into SoroVista — `classifySearch` routes a query to either a contract page or an event page — and the typical session is a loop of paste an identifier, read, paste another. For a tool used that way, a shortcut to focus the search field is the difference between a two-second task and a five-second one, repeated all day.

The templates are small and self-contained, which keeps this bounded.

## Requirements and context

This is scoped to be completable within a single Wave cycle and to pass CI on its own — it does not depend on any other open issue unless stated above.

- Repository: `sorotrail/SoroVista`
- Contributor setup and test prerequisites: `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- Issue conventions: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
- Primary files: `internal/web/templates/layout.html`, `internal/web/templates/index.html`, `internal/web/handlers.go`

## Suggested execution

1. Comment on this issue to be assigned before you start, so two people don't duplicate the work.
2. Fork the repository and create a branch:
   ```
   git checkout -b web-keyboard-shortcuts
   ```
3. Make the change described under **Implementation guidance**.
4. Run the commands under **Testing** and confirm they pass.
5. Commit using the format under **Example commit message**, push, and open a PR against `main`.

## What "done" looks like

- A shortcut focuses the search box from anywhere on the page, following the convention people already expect from other developer tools: `/` to focus search, and `Escape` to blur it and clear focus.
- The shortcut does **not** fire while the user is typing in an input, a textarea or any editable field. Hijacking `/` mid-query is the way this feature becomes annoying rather than useful.
- A discoverable list of shortcuts, reachable by `?`, rendered as a small overlay or a short section. A shortcut nobody can find is not a feature.
- Navigation shortcuts for the handful of pages that exist — the index, the contracts list — chosen so they do not collide with browser or screen-reader bindings.
- Browser defaults are not overridden. `Ctrl+F`, `Cmd+L` and the like must keep working; intercepting them is a hard no.
- Accessible: shortcuts are an addition, not a replacement. Everything stays reachable by `Tab`, focus outlines remain visible, and the overlay traps focus correctly and is dismissible by `Escape`.
- Works without a build step. No framework, no new dependency, and a small amount of inline script consistent with the rest of the UI.
- Degrades silently if script is unavailable: the page must remain fully usable.

## Implementation guidance

- `layout.html` carries the shared head and is where a single global key handler belongs, so each page does not need its own.
- Check the event target before acting. The usual guard is to ignore the key when the active element is an input, a textarea, a select or anything with `contenteditable` set.
- Prefer `event.key` over the deprecated `keyCode`, and do not call `preventDefault` unless you are actually handling the key.
- Keep the shortcut set small. Three or four bindings people remember beat a dozen nobody does.
- If the dark-mode issue has landed, reuse its colour tokens for the overlay rather than hard-coding colours, so the overlay works in both schemes.
- Do not add a command palette. That is a much larger feature and would deserve its own issue.

## Testing

Run the checks CI runs, from the repository root:

```
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test ./...
golangci-lint run
```

The new or changed behaviour must be covered by a test that fails if it regresses. Confirm that by temporarily breaking the code and re-running.

Database-backed tests need Postgres: `make up` then `make test-db`. Without `TEST_DATABASE_URL` the tests in `internal/store/postgres_test.go` skip rather than fail, so a green local run without it does not prove the store paths work.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs build, `go vet`, the test suite, a second test pass against a Postgres service container, and `golangci-lint` (pinned to v2.12.2, configured in `.golangci.yml`).

## Example commit message

```
feat(dashboard): keyboard shortcuts for search and navigation

<why this change is needed and anything non-obvious about how>

Closes #44
```

## Guidelines

- Complexity: **Trivial (100 points)**. If the work turns out materially larger than this once you are in the code, say so on the issue rather than absorbing it — the tag should be corrected, not quietly outgrown.
- Comment to be assigned first; unassigned PRs may duplicate someone else's work.
- The PR description must link this issue (`Closes #44`) and state what you changed and how you verified it.
- Keep the PR to this issue's scope. Unrelated fixes you spot along the way are welcome as separate issues or PRs.
- CI must be green before review: build, vet, tests and lint.
- Upstream mode (`SOURCE_MODE=sorotrail`) must keep working: it opens no database, so nothing on a read path may assume Postgres is present.
- `source.EventSource` is the only seam the API and web layers see — keep backend details behind it.
- Structured logging via `log/slog` with `lower_snake_case` keys.
- Match the surrounding code: this codebase favours full-sentence comments that explain *why*, not restatements of the code.
- If anything here is ambiguous, ask on the issue before building — a question costs less than a rewritten PR.

items.title: feat(dashboard): relative timestamps and copy-to-clipboard for identifiers

labels.name: complexity:trivial
labels.description: Small, bounded change with obvious criteria (100 points)

items.body:
## Description

Two small frictions in the UI, both reachable from the same set of templates.

**Timestamps are absolute only.** Events carry `LedgerClosedAt`, the on-chain close time, and the templates render it as-is. The question a visitor actually has is "how long ago", and working that out from a UTC timestamp is mental arithmetic on every row.

**Identifiers cannot be copied.** Contract IDs are 56-character strkeys and event IDs are TOIDs, and the tables deliberately abbreviate them through the `shorten` helper — `{{shorten .ContractID 6}}` in the event rows, `{{shorten .ID 10}}` in the contract list. So the full value is visible only in a `title` attribute or by navigating to the detail page, and selecting it by hand from a monospace cell is fiddly and error-prone. These identifiers exist to be pasted into another tool.

## Requirements and context

This is scoped to be completable within a single Wave cycle and to pass CI on its own — it does not depend on any other open issue unless stated above.

- Primary files: `internal/web/templates/partials.html`, `internal/web/templates/contract.html`, `internal/web/templates/event.html`, `internal/web/web.go`

## Suggested execution

1. Comment on this issue to be assigned before you start, so two people don't duplicate the work.
2. Fork the repository and create a branch:
   ```
   git checkout -b web-timestamps-and-copy
   ```
3. Make the change described under **Implementation guidance**.
4. Run the commands under **Testing** and confirm they pass.
5. Commit using the format under **Example commit message**, push, and open a PR against `main`.

## What "done" looks like

- Event and contract rows show a relative time (`4m ago`, `2h ago`, `3d ago`) with the exact timestamp available on hover through a `title` attribute. Both pieces of information stay reachable; the relative form is what is read at a glance.
- The distinction between the two timestamps is preserved. `LedgerClosedAt` is on-chain time and `CreatedAt` is when SoroVista ingested the row, and the schema keeps them deliberately separate. Do not silently relabel one as the other — show the chain time, and say which it is.
- A copy control next to each abbreviated identifier that copies the **full** value, not the shortened display form.
- Copy gives visible confirmation, and fails gracefully. The clipboard API needs a secure context, so an instance served over plain HTTP will not have it — the control must not appear broken there, and a fallback or a hidden control are both acceptable if chosen deliberately.
- Works on the contract list, the event rows partial, the contract detail page and the event detail page. These are easy to fix in one template and forget in another.
- Accessible: the control has a label, is reachable by keyboard, and the confirmation is announced rather than being colour-only.
- No new dependency and no CSS framework. The relative-time formatting can be done server-side in a template function or client-side in a few lines.
- Relative times do not go stale on a long-open page, or the staleness is bounded and acknowledged. A page left open for an hour showing "2m ago" is worse than an absolute time.

## Implementation guidance

- `templateFuncs()` in `internal/web/web.go` is where a `relativeTime` helper belongs, alongside the existing `render`, `shorten` and `summary` functions.
- Server-side formatting is simplest but freezes at render time; client-side updates stay fresh but need the absolute value in the markup anyway. Pick one, and if you go server-side, say how you handled staleness — the event feed partial already refreshes, which may solve it for free.
- Note that `shorten` currently truncates by byte offset and can emit invalid UTF-8; there is a separate issue for that. Do not fix it here, and do not build the copy control in a way that depends on the shortened value being well-formed.
- Keep the diff to the templates, the template functions and a small amount of inline script. A UI restructuring is not this issue.

labels.name: complexity:trivial
labels.description: Small, bounded change with obvious criteria (100 points)

items.body:
## Description

The deployment documentation covers containers. There is nothing about running SoroVista as a plain systemd service, and no unit file to start from.

That matters because SoroVista's own positioning points that way. It is a single static binary with CGO disabled, and in upstream mode it needs no database at all — so the smallest sensible deployment is one binary on one small VPS, watching one contract. Someone doing that has to work out the unit file, the environment-file layout, the user and the hardening options themselves.

SoroBeacon has the same gap filed as its own issue, so the two pages should end up consistent.

## Requirements and context

## Description

The API adds a `token` field to event responses when an event matches the SEP-41 token layout, resolving the event into named slots so a client can say that X sent Y to Z without knowing the topic positions. It is one of the most useful things SoroVista does with a decoded event.

## Description

The documentation covers installation, configuration, both operating modes and deployment, but there is no page for the thing a new operator actually hits: it started, and the explorer is empty.
